messages:
Aisha: Starting a focused RFC follow-up: extract the policy-plane (rate/quotas, tenant rules, feature gates) out of control-plane into a separate service. Goal: reduce blast radius on hotpath and make policy changes deployable without control-plane rollouts. Thought: keep policy evaluation sync for hotpath, async for long-running policies.

Dmitri: Strong +1. Main risks: cross-service latency, cache churn, and consistency during migration. Do we want a read-through cache in the request runtime or stick with a tiny local policy cache + remote check?

Hannah: Preference for tiny local TTL cache (50ms staleness budget) on hotpath + fallback remote call. That keeps p95 impact low. For write path (policy update), use eventual consistency with versioned policy IDs so requester can detect version drift. Also will need a changefeed to invalidate caches.

Aisha: Proposed migration plan (high level):
- define clear policy API (eval(policy_key, context) -> decision + policy_version) + schema docs
- implement policy-service v1 behind feature flag `feature.policy_plane_v1`
- add changefeed from policy-store -> policy-service -> push invalidation stream to runtimes
- start with shadow evals for 14 days, compare decisions with control-plane (diff tolerant on non-deterministic rules)
- enable canary 5% with local cache TTL=100ms and remote timeout 30ms, monitor errors
- expand canary and reduce TTL to target 50ms if stable

Sam: Important to add a golden-path contract test: replay a window of traffic (sampled) and assert decisions are identical for deterministic rules. Non-deterministic rules should have a classification mapping so differences are acceptable if within threshold.

Dmitri: For the changefeed, consider using existing pubsub infra (we already have tenant-topics). But ensure we have high fanout protections - policy churn could slam runtimes. Maybe aggregate invalidations into short windows (debounce 200ms).

Hannah: Observability requirements: trace across the new boundary, expose decision latency histogram and cache hit ratio, and a comparator metric: fraction_of_different_decisions_on_shadow. Create an APM dashboard and alert if diff_rate > 0.5% for 1h.

Aisha: Good call. Also adding rollback strategy: if p95 increases >8% or error rate >0.2% above baseline, flip feature flag to route to legacy. Also enforce a cost guardrail: simulated fanout test before any >10% rollout.

Sam: Ownership: I'll own policy API contract and test harness. Dmitri will spike the changefeed and caching semantics. Hannah will own observability and the comparator dashboard. Aisha will coordinate rollout checklist and docs.

Aisha: Minimal sample API we can doc in the README:
```
POST /v1/eval
{
  "policy_key": "rate_limit:tenant:default",
  "ctx": {"tenant_id":"t123","route":"/v1/generate","tokens":10}
}
=> {"decision":"allow","policy_version":"v12","meta":{"ttl_ms":100}}
```
Also include a health endpoint that returns policy_version and last_changefeed_ts.

Deploy-bot: started shadow deployment: policy-service v1 (id: shadow-221000)

Dmitri: Quick note: ensure we have a durable audit log for policy changes for compliance. It should include before/after and the author. We'll need a retention policy for compliance teams.

Hannah: I'll add the comparator to the CI (non-blocking) so PRs that change policy eval code run a tiny replay against the harness. Fail thresholds documented.

Aisha: I'll open GH issues: 1) API spec + README; 2) contract-harness spike; 3) changefeed spike; 4) dashboard + alerts; 5) rollout checklist + cost sim. Linking here when created. Let's reconvene after the spikes in two weeks.

Sam: Thanks 44d. Short-term action: Sam/Dmitri/Hannah sync tomorrow to align on invalidation semantics and debouncing.

Aisha: perfect. One last ops note: set default remote timeout conservative (30ms) and circuit-breaker to fail-open to legacy behavior for safety.

Dmitri: noted. Will prototype a small simulator to validate cache hit ratio vs TTL tradeoffs and share numbers in the spike PR.

Hannah: copying ops/security on audit retention and RBAC surface for policy mutations.

Aisha: End of thread: thanks team.
